title: Permission Scenario Engine + Audit Playbook for RBAC v2
creator: Asha Kapoor
description: Build a reusable Permission Scenario Engine and an accompanying Audit Playbook to increase confidence in RBAC v2 changes. The engine will generate deterministic and mutation-based permission test vectors (cross-tenant, cross-role, and admin-edge cases), run them against the runtime access checks and the audit log pipeline, and assert both enforcement and audit fidelity. The playbook documents how to triage audit mismatches, reproduce live incidents, and add new golden fixtures. Goals: 1) Replace brittle hand-written tests with scenario-driven fixtures that cover common and adversarial flows; 2) Surface gaps in audit logging (missing fields, truncated metadata, SAML/SSO attribution issues); 3) Gate RBAC v2 rollouts with a regression suite that runs in CI and nightly cluster-level sweeps. Constraints: must run against Hosted/Dedicated/Private stack variants, avoid exposing real PII (use synthetic tenant IDs), and complete runs within CI time budgets by sampling and prioritizing scenarios. Acceptance criteria: a) Scenario engine produces a canonical JSON manifest per fixture and a minimized replay recipe for CI; b) CI job "rbac-perm-scenarios" runs and fails on any enforcement or audit regression for the runtime-1.20 release branch; c) Playbook published to Confluence with step-by-step reproduction and a triage checklist; d) At least 150 unique scenarios covering admin impersonation, cross-tenant reads, write-deny over wildcard, SAML attribute-mapped roles, and audit-field completeness.
acceptance_criteria: Canonical JSON manifest format defined and documented in repository README

notes: Design trade-offs: Deterministic fixtures give traceability and easy minimization; fuzzing finds complex interactions but increases noise — we separate them into CI vs nightly lanes.
Open risks: Cross-tenant test scaffolding may be complex for Private deployments with different network topologies. We will provide an isolated network harness (see infra task in attachments).
Performance consideration: Full sweep across all roles and tenants is combinatorial — implement risk-based sampling and an importance-weighted scheduler.
Follow-ups: Integrate with Console's rollouts to auto-run impacted scenarios on canary traffic and report regressions to the rollout dashboard.
